question: How is BlockSuite, the editor framework under `blocksuite/`, structured: what are its main packages and kinds of components, and how does the AFFiNE app use it?

points.text: BlockSuite has two groups of packages: a headless framework (`blocksuite/framework`: `@blocksuite/store`, `@blocksuite/std` and support packages) and the prebuilt editing components built on it (`blocksuite/affine`: the blocks, widgets, fragments, models and shared code); the framework does not depend on the components
`@blocksuite/store` is the data layer: documents are modeled on the Yjs CRDT, which gives them real-time collaboration and history (undo/redo)

`@blocksuite/std` (the docs' `block-std`) is the standard library for editable blocks: UI event handling, selection and clipboard (with commands), and the `EditorHost` that turns the block tree into components
rich text is handled by a small inline editor (the docs' `@blocksuite/inline`): each block's text is its own Y.Text with its own inline editor, instead of one rich-text editor for the whole document

its component types are editors (the page editor and the edgeless whiteboard editor), blocks, widgets (helper UI that shows up for a block, such as the slash menu or drag handle) and fragments (UI outside the editor that shares its document, such as the doc title or outline panel)
all of these components are native web components built with lit, while the AFFiNE app is written in React, so the app wraps BlockSuite's editors in React components

an editor is thin, just the set of block and widget registrations mounted on an `EditorHost`; so the page and edgeless editors are two views of the same document, and the root block keeps one model (`RootBlockModel`, flavour `affine:page`) with a different view in each
BlockSuite stands apart from the app, like Monaco from VS Code: the app depends on BlockSuite and reuses it through its components, and BlockSuite never imports the app's code

answer:
BlockSuite lives in `blocksuite/`. It has a small framework layer and a large set of AFFiNE-specific packages built on it. This comes from the directory layout and a few file counts. I didn't read the code in depth.

**Framework (`blocksuite/framework/`)**
- `global`: shared utilities. These cover dependency injection (`di`), disposables, env, exceptions, lit helpers and gfx types.
- `store`: the document data layer. It holds the schema, block models, reactive state, transformers, adapters and store extensions.
- `std`: the editor runtime. It covers the view layer, commands, events, selection, clipboard, inline text, gfx (the edgeless canvas) and the extension and spec system.
- `sync`: a third package under `framework/` that I didn't open.

**AFFiNE layer (`blocksuite/affine/`)**
- `model`: the block and element schemas.
- `blocks/*`: one package per block type, such as paragraph, list, code, database, table, image, attachment, embed, note, frame and surface. `root` is also here.
- `gfx/*`: edgeless tools and elements, including brush, connector, shape, mindmap, text, group and template. There is also a `turbo-renderer`.
- `widgets/*`: UI overlays such as the slash menu, toolbars, drag handle, linked-doc and remote-selection.
- `fragments/*`: side panels such as outline, frame panel, doc title and adapter panel.
- `inlines`, `rich-text`, `components`, `data-view`, `shared` and `foundation`: shared building blocks.
- `ext-loader`: loads extensions.
- `all`: an aggregator package.

**Supporting folders**
- `playground`: a dev app.
- `integration-test`: the integration tests.
- `docs` and `docs-site`: documentation.

**Component kinds**
- Models, which are the data schemas.
- Block views, which are lit web components.
- Extensions, which are DI-registered and wire everything together.
- Widgets and fragments.
- Adapters, which convert to and from markdown, HTML and similar formats.
- Gfx tools and elements.

**How AFFiNE uses it**
- The app's code is in `packages/frontend/core/src/blocksuite/`. Its subfolders include `editors`, `block-suite-editor`, `view-extensions`, `store-extensions`, `manager`, `initialization`, `ai`, `attachment-viewer`, `outline-viewer` and `database-block`.
- It composes the editor by supplying its own store and view extensions: `store-extensions` and `view-extensions` hold app-specific specs for storage and rendering.
- It also adds app features on top, mainly the AI chat panel and the page and mode-switch UI.
- The dependency is wide. About 391 files under `packages/frontend/core/src` import `@blocksuite/affine*` packages.
